topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture and states what students should learn about cancer treatments.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how local treatments remove or destroy tumors and how chemotherapy supports their effectiveness.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains the effectiveness and limitations of drugs that damage cancer cells but also affect healthy dividing cells.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This material shows how blocking required hormonal signals can suppress breast and prostate cancer growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how missing checkpoint proteins create selective vulnerabilities to irradiation and oncolytic viruses.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how inhibiting a remaining DNA repair pathway selectively kills cancer cells already deficient in BRCA-mediated repair.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and targeted kinase inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how identifying the oncogenic driver of a tumor enables treatment directed at its essential growth machinery.

topics.label: Limitations and resistance in kinase inhibitor treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why kinase inhibition often becomes long-term disease control rather than a cure and how treatment must adapt to resistant tumor populations.

topics.label: Antibody therapies targeting cancer-cell surface proteins
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how antibody recognition of surface proteins directs therapeutic activity toward cancer cells.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This material evaluates whether the body's existing immune system protects against cancer.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint blockade and tumor neoantigens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade restores antitumor T-cell activity and why recognition of tumor neoantigens influences its effectiveness.

topics.label: Redirecting T cells with bispecific engagers and CAR T cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe engineered approaches that direct T-cell cytotoxicity toward selected tumor antigens.

topics.label: Treatment challenges and biomarker-guided cancer care
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains why matching treatment to a patient's evolving cancer is essential but remains difficult.

topics.label: Cancer outcome trends, prevention and early detection
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines how prevention and earlier diagnosis complicate the interpretation of improvements in cancer outcomes.

topics.label: Future treatment priorities and ethical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: This material considers how future cancer care should balance opportunities for improvement against treatment burdens and patient quality of life.

topics.label: Concluding case: childhood leukemia survival and trials of new therapies
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding case uses the success of cytotoxic treatment in childhood leukemia to illustrate the dilemma of testing newer therapies against highly effective established care.
